column1: # Grayscale fast path vs general quantizer (zenquant) — issue #4 validation
# date: 2026-06-13   host: lilith   zengif commit: 61c9fcb (incl. mid-stream-flush fix)
# CORPUS / METHOD: /mnt/v/imazen-26, all 1069 images scanned for strictly
#   grayscale content by EXACT full-resolution R==G==B (Pillow). 28 qualify.
#   (An earlier ImageMagick HSL-saturation probe was unreliable — it false-
#    positived 4 vividly-colored images and false-negatived ~16 real ones —
# A_gray  = encode_gif (gray fast path, lossless by construction)
#   - Speed: gray path ~8.5x faster mean (≈8x photos/patents, ≈13-16x doc scans).
#   - Lossless: A on 28/28; quantizer only on 9/28 (the 2-level images). On the
#     19 continuous-tone images the gray path is lossless where zenquant is not.
#   - Size: A is NEVER smaller (0/28); +0.16% total, worst +2.6% (one chart).
#     The 'gray is smaller' guess was wrong; the win is speed + losslessness.
#   - This run also surfaced the mid-stream-flush bug (logan-voss, 33MP/256-level
#     was lossy pre-fix); fixed in commit 61c9fcb, lossless here.
